author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Concord High’s defense controlled Friday night’s game in Hudson, helping the Crimson Tide defeat Alvirne 37-7. The game remained scoreless until the final 34 seconds of the first half, but Concord broke it open after halftime with two touchdowns and a safety in the third quarter.

The Crimson Tide finished with 15 tackles for loss, six sacks and a fumble recovery. Jax Diachenko led the pressure with 3.5 sacks, three tackles for loss and the safety. Sebastian Telus added five tackles for loss and two sacks, while Michael Gamache contributed three tackles for loss and a half-sack. Dustin Ellis forced and recovered a fumble.

On offense, Colin Savard carried 21 times for 176 yards. Quarterback Rhys Craigue completed eight of 19 passes for 142 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown to Methuselah Doe. A 50-yard gain by Savard on a short reception helped set up that score. Concord’s combination of backfield disruption and a steady rushing attack turned a tight first half into a decisive road victory.
dek: The Crimson Tide recorded 15 tackles for loss and six sacks before pulling away with two touchdowns and a safety in the third quarter.
headline: Concord defense powers 37-7 win over Alvirne
